newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi shares begin trading at $15 in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi shares begin trading at $15 in Beirut.

text.p: Shares in Banque Audi were traded for the first time on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday at $15 on turnover of 10,000 shares.

Audi, the second Lebanese commercial bank to list on BSE, has offered all its 4,158,000 C shares -- or 30 percent of its total number of shares -- for trading on the market. The bank shares have a nominal value of 2,000 Lebanese pounds ($1.29).
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce closed unchanged from Friday's $12.375 on trade of 1,500 shares against 2,000.

BLC was the first bank to list its shares on the exchange since it reopened last year after a 13-year shutdown due to Lebanon's civil war. BLC has been a star performer since it began trading December 30.
Also on the BSE, Solidere A shares recovered to $10.5 from Friday's record low of $10.25. Solidere B shares fell to $11.125 from Friday's $11.25.
Turnover in Solidere was 33,446 from 33,105 on Friday and value was $358,321.5 from $310,614.75.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index rose 0.14 percent to 81.10 and the BLOM stock index rose 0.38 percent to 912.58.
